classification.difficultyReason: Development: students use the key and the supplied distance-horizontal, time-vertical axes to read two finishing times, then estimate both times at 75 metres and compare them. This links routine graph readings while adapting the taught reading method to a different axis arrangement.

content.prompt:
Melinda and Cathy are running a $100\text{ m}$ sprint.
They wear smartwatches to track their distance over time.

spec.description: Unshaded sprint graph with distance horizontal, time vertical, two black broken traces and an external boxed key. No separate point markers.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal range 0–100 metres with grid every 5 metres; vertical range 0–20 seconds with grid every 2 seconds. Cathy ends at (100,20); Melinda ends at (100,16). Interior trace coordinates reconstruct visual observations, not an asserted function or exact dataset. At 75 metres the readings are approximately 15 and 10 seconds.
spec.answerVisibility: Both source traces and the key are permanent question givens; no answer-reading guides are added.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How long did it take Melinda to finish the race?

answer.worked: At $100\text{ m}$, Melinda’s long-dashed trace reads $16\text{ s}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How long did it take Cathy to finish the race?

answer.worked: At $100\text{ m}$, Cathy’s dotted trace reads $20\text{ s}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: How long after Melinda did Cathy pass the $75$ metre mark in the race?

answer.worked:
At $75\text{ m}$, Cathy’s time is approximately $15\text{ s}$ and Melinda’s is approximately $10\text{ s}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Time difference}&\approx 15-10\\&=5\text{ s}\end{align*}$$
